articles.description: NORTH LIBERTY, Iowa, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Heartland Express, Inc. (www.heartlandexpress.com) (HTLD) is pleased to announce that Chairman and CEO Michael Gerdin will ring the Closing Bell at the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square on Tuesday, November 10. The ceremony will recognize the 40th listing anniversary on the Nasdaq Stock Market and the 48th anniversary as a premier truckload transportation company. Joining Mr. Gerdin on stage will be more than 50 employees including professional truck drivers, founding family members, company leaders, long-term employees, and members of the board of directors. Mike Gerdin, CEO stated, "It is with great pride that we recognize this honor on behalf of our professional drivers, our supporting employees, and our stockholders for forty-eight years as a company and forty years as a publicly traded company on the Nasdaq Stock Market. Through the years, we have remained committed to and worked hard to deliver ‘Service for Success’ to our customers. That commitment is made possible by our tremendous professional drivers and supporting employees.” Founded in 1978 by Russell Gerdin and headquartered in North Liberty, Iowa, Heartland Express has built an enduring legacy on a simple foundation: a commitment to safe, reliable service delivered by exceptional professional drivers. For more than four decades, that commitment has made Heartland a trusted partner to retailers, manufacturers, and shippers across the country. articles.title: Climate Rioters Storm Microsoft Data Center Site In Amsterdam, Chant "Free Palestine" & "F**k AI"
articles.description: Climate Rioters Storm Microsoft Data Center Site In Amsterdam, Chant "Free Palestine" & "F**k AI" Far-left climate activists broke into the construction site of a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam earlier this morning. The breach is a troubling sign that far-left social unrest across the West is far from over. Geef Tegengas, a Dutch direct-action collective that began targeting fossil gas infrastructure in 2024, led the breach at the Amsterdam data center construction site. The action comes as this year's energy crisis exposes a key vulnerability in Europe's transition away from fossil fuels: demand for natural gas persists, leaving households and industry exposed to supply disruptions and price spikes. Around 100 Geef Tegengas comrades entered the construction site, Reuters reported. Some carried signs reading "f*ck AI" and "Microsoft powers genocide." Protesters also chanted "Microsoft has got to go" and "free Palestine." So who funds Geef Tegengas? Dutch news coverage of the group's 2024 launch identified Patagonia, the Climate Emergency Fund, Fossielvrij NL and Stichting Vrienden van XR as co-funders. Fossielvrij NL launched the movement. Who financed this morning's protest remains unclear. Patagonia Action Works links Geef Tegengas. The backlash against data centers across the West is particularly troubling given the Trump administration's plans to expand the US power grid, rebuild the industrial base, and accelerate economic growth to escape the country's debt trap. Yet the Democrats in the US, who have joined forces with socialists and socialist reformists, are attempting to derail the buildout and pop the investment cycle. In Amsterdam, far-left activists had their list of causes, protesting both the environmental cost of data centers and Microsoft's ties to Israel. That raises a broader question: Who stands to benefit if the West fails to build data centers and power plants it needs to revitalize a hallowed-out industrial base? Well, that question also surfaced in the US earlier this summer, when a report alleged that a China-linked NGO was amplifying opposition to data centers ahead of the midterm elections. By Election Day, data centers had become the top concern for many voters. Tyler Durden Fri, 11/06/2026 - 12:40

articles.title: BSP says forex market stable amid peso slump
articles.description: THE Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) said adequate international reserves and continued inflows from remittances and business process outsourcing (BPO) service exports are helping support foreign-exchange market stability amid the peso’s depreciation. BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja made the statement on Friday, as the Philippine peso hit a record low of P64.17 against the US dollar on Oct. 27. Despite the currency's decline, Abenoja said dollar inflows continued to help meet the foreign-currency needs of businesses and households. He added that the BSP has been monitoring market developments and potential inflationary effects from exchange-rate movements. The central bank also stressed that the country's international reserves remained more than adequate, while remittances from overseas Filipinos continued to grow, although at a slower pace. BPO revenues likewise continued to increase, providing another source of foreign exchange earnings for the country. “All of these continue to support stability in the foreign exchange market,” Abenoja said in a press briefing on the economic and investment briefing in Iloilo City. Abenoja added that BSP is closely monitoring developments in the foreign exchange market and would work to maintain orderly conditions. “We want the foreign exchange market to experience orderly conditions,” said Abenoja. “We want the market to be able to serve the requirements of our growing economy. That is one of our main goals,” he added. He assured the public that the central bank is watching for possible inflationary effects arising from significant exchange-rate movements, which could add to existing price pressures. “We will endeavor to support market functioning so that we can serve the needs of our business and our households in terms of foreign exchange,” Abenoja said.
